title: torch.no_grad() yields NaN values on mps device, 4D attention mask
bug_description: ### 🐛 Describe the bug on macOS, define a 4D attention mask that is padded, and call a model. ```py @pytest.mark.parametrize("device", ["cpu", "mps"]) def test_isolated_language_model_mps(device): model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("sbintuitions/tiny-lm").to(device) input_ids = torch.tensor([[0, 1, 0, 0], [0, 1, 2, 3]], device=device) attention_mask = torch.tensor([ [[[ True, False, False, False], [ True, True, False, False], [False, False, False, False], [False, False, False, False]]], [[[ True, False, False, False], [ True, True, False, False], [ True, True, True, False], [ True, True, True, True]]]], device=device) # attention_mask = torch.tensor([[1, 1, 0, 0], [1, 1, 1, 1]], dtype=torch.bool, device=device) with torch.no_grad(): outputs = model(input_ids=input_ids, attention_mask=attention_mask) assert not torch.isnan(outputs.logits).any(), "Logits contain NaN values" ``` ### Expected behavior not NaN - same as it is on CPU. Also, if removing `torch.no_grad()` it is also not NaN. ### Versions Collecting environment information... @pytest.mark.parametrize("device", ["cpu", "mps"])
def test_isolated_language_model_mps(device):
    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("sbintuitions/tiny-lm").to(device)
    input_ids = torch.tensor([[0, 1, 0, 0], [0, 1, 2, 3]], device=device)

    attention_mask = torch.tensor([
        [[[ True, False, False, False],
          [ True,  True, False, False],
          [False, False, False, False],
          [False, False, False, False]]],
        [[[ True, False, False, False],
          [ True,  True, False, False],
          [ True,  True,  True, False],
          [ True,  True,  True,  True]]]], device=device)
    # attention_mask = torch.tensor([[1, 1, 0, 0], [1, 1, 1, 1]], dtype=torch.bool, device=device)

    with torch.no_grad():
       outputs = model(input_ids=input_ids, attention_mask=attention_mask)
    assert not torch.isnan(outputs.logits).any(), "Logits contain NaN values"
error_description: On macOS, using a 4D attention mask that is padded and calling a model within a torch.no_grad() context yields NaN values on the MPS device. This does not happen on CPU, and it does not happen on MPS if torch.no_grad() is removed.
